item.title: U.S. Commerce Dept. Inquiry Into Megaspeed Was Halted After Nvidia Intervention
item.description: An investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore company that was buying advanced Nvidia A.I. chips, was transferred to the Justice Department after a top Nvidia executive reached out to Commerce Department officials.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson and Devlin Barrett
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Nvidia said on Sunday that it was opening an investigation into Jensen Huang, after he acknowledged he had been intimate with an executive at a Singaporean company suspected of smuggling chips into China.

item.title: Is Jensen Huang Too Powerful to Be Punished by Nvidia?
item.description: The chief executive has a tight grip on his company, presenting a challenge for Nvidia’s board, which is investigating his affair with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang and Tripp Mickle
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang is Nvidia’s biggest individual shareholder. His children are also senior executives at the company.

item.title: Nvidia’s Stock Price Drops After Investigation Into CEO Jensen Huang

item.title: An Anti-Trump Protest. Police Threats. Inside a Rift in Diabetes Research.

item.title: Martin Luther King’s Lost Draft of ‘I Have a Dream’ Speech Surfaces
item.description: The document, hand written by Martin Luther King Jr., will be auctioned in January at Christie’s, which expects it to fetch more than $10 million.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler
item.category: Center for Civil and Human Rights (Atlanta, Ga)
item.media:credit: Bettman Archive, via Getty Images
item.media:description: The Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. improvised the storied “I have a dream” section of his speech at the March on Washington in August 1963. A recently surfaced draft shows the version he wrote out in longhand the night before.
